Text 1

My most valuable possession is an old, slightly warped blond guitar--the first instrument I taught myself how to play.

It's nothing fancy, just a Madeira folk guitar, all scuffed and scratched and finger-printed. At the top is a bramble of copper-wound strings, each one hooked through the eye of a silver tuning key. The strings are stretched down a long, slim neck, its frets tarnished, and the wood worn by years of fingers pressing chords and picking notes. The body of the Madeira is shaped like an enormous yellow pear, one that was slightly damaged in shipping. The blond wood has been chipped and gouged to gray, particularly where the pick guard fell off years ago.

No, it's not a beautiful instrument, but it still lets me make music, and for that I will always treasure it.

What does the text tell you about?
options: The writer's first music play
The writer's first treasure
The writer's first guitar
The writer's first pear
rationale: The text describes the writer's old Madeira folk guitar and states that it was the first instrument the writer learned to play. Therefore, the text is about the writer's first guitar.

Text 3

The Lion and the Mouse

Once upon a time, there was a fierce Lion that ruled the wood. One day, when the Lion was trying to take a nap, a Mouse running over his face awakened the Lion from sleep. Rising up angrily, he caught him and was about to kill him. Then the Mouse piteously entreated, saying:

"If you would only spare my life, I would be sure to repay your kindness." The Lion laughed at him but allowed him to go. It happened shortly after this that some hunters, who bound him by strong ropes to the ground, caught the Lion. The Mouse, recognizing his roar, came and gnawed the rope with his teeth, and set him free, exclaiming:

"You ridiculed the idea of my ever being able to help you, never expecting to receive from me any repayment of your favor. Now you know that it is possible for even a Mouse to confer benefits on a Lion."

According to the text, when did the Lion and the Mouse meet each other? It was when ...
options: the Lion caught by the hunters
the Mouse heard the Lion roared
the Mouse ran over the Lion's face
When the Mouse was trying to save the Lion
rationale: The first meeting happens when the Lion is sleeping and the Mouse runs over his face. This wakes the Lion up.

Text 4

How to Make a Fabric Fan

Things you'll need to prepare:
- Cotton cloth fabric
- Scissors
- Measuring tape
- Tacky glue
- Craft sticks
- Drill
- Drill bit, 1/16-inch
- Brass brad

Instructions:
(1) Cut a rectangle shape from cotton cloth fabric using scissors to measure 6 inches wide and 18 inches long. Select any colors or pattern of fabric that you want.
(2) Lay the cloth horizontally onto the top of a table and fold the left edge over by 1 inch. Press the fold flat using your hand.
(3) Apply tacky glue onto the back side of the fold. Next, press a craft stick onto the glue-covered fold. Line up the craft stick so the top edge of it is flat with the top edge of the fabric. Let the glue dry for twenty minutes.
(4) Fold the fabric by 1-inch on the left side again. This time, fold the fabric in the opposite direction. You can press the fold flat with your hand. Put some tacky glue onto the back side of the fold. Next, press another craft stick onto the glue-covered fold. Repeat this process until you have folded and glued on craft sticks along the whole length.
(5) Drill a small hole using a small size drill bit into the end of each craft stick. After that, stack the sticks on top of each other. Insert a brass brad into the sack over the drilled holes and bend the brad once through to secure it into place.
(6) Splay out the stacked craft sticks to lengthen the fabric hand fan.

"Lay the cloth horizontally onto the top of a table..." What does the underlined word nearly mean?
options: put something down into a flat position
bring something up to the higher surface
take something out into a certain place
give something in to the secured position
rationale: In the instruction, lay means placing the cloth flat on the table before folding it. The closest meaning is to put something down into a flat position.
